[Arabic academic text, translated for reference] ...or his claim of divinity for him. Then the last era of the Companions was during the governance of Ibn al-Zubayr and Abd al-Malik. Then the heresy of the Murji'a and the Qadariyya arose, and in the late Umayyad caliphate the heresy of the Jahmiyya and the anthropomorphist (Mushabbiha) sect arose, and none of this existed in the era of the Companions. Likewise the trials (fitan) of the sword: the people were united during the governorship of Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, fighting the enemy together. When Mu'awiyah died, Husayn was killed, and Ibn al-Zubayr was besieged in Makkah (2). Then the trial of the Harra occurred in Medina, then the trial of Yazid's death occurred in Syria between Marwan and al-Dahhak ibn Qays. Then al-Mukhtar rose up against Ibn Ziyad and killed him, and a trial occurred. Then Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr came and killed al-Mukhtar, and a trial occurred. Then Abd al-Malik went out against Mus'ab and killed him, and a trial occurred. He sent al-Hajjaj to besiege Ibn al-Zubayr for a period until he killed him, and a trial occurred. Then when al-Hajjaj took charge of Iraq, Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath rose up against him with a great following from the people of Iraq, and it was a huge trial; this was after the death of Mu'awiyah. Then a trial occurred [involving] Ibn al-Muhallab in Khurasan, and Zayd ibn Ali was killed in Kufa and many others were killed, then Abu Muslim arose in Khurasan and elsewhere, and wars and trials occurred and their description lengthens (3).

And in light of this, we do not consider it far-fetched that this state of affairs [i.e., fabrication of hadith] existed before the appearance of the great trial (fitna), just as we do not consider it far-fetched that some among the Companions might voluntarily fabricate hadith upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and it is not conceivable that a Muslim would imagine that the noble, illustrious Companions, who sacrificed themselves and their wealth in the path of Allah [and text continues onto next page]...

[Arabic academic text, translated for reference] ...explicit hadiths in support of political doctrines and religious sects, and fabricated hadiths were born together with the emergence of these sects, just as those who defended [certain positions] against opponents would fabricate hadiths refuting them, and so on, until a whole body of fabricated hadith accumulated, which the scholars of this science and its experts have since exposed. Fabrication was not limited to the merits of individuals, and support of opinions and doctrinal ideas and political schools; rather it extended to cover the various chapters of hadith literature, and fabricated hadiths came to address all aspects of life, private and public. Hadiths were fabricated concerning virtues and vices, hadiths on the merits of various lands and days, and others concerning different acts of worship, in transactions, food, literature, asceticism, remembrance (dhikr), supplication, medicine, illness, trials (fitan), inheritance law, and other topics.

It is worth noting that this state of affairs did not reach its peak until this [later] century, because it had begun shortly before the middle of the first Hijri century, and forgery was quickly recognized by the Companions and the Followers (Tabi'in) who knew and preserved hadith, and they were not misled by the fabrications of liars or the reports of forgers. This points to the fact that the causes of this phenomenon in that century were not numerous, and fabricated hadith did not increase in step with the growth of heresy (bid'ah) and dissension, and the senior Companions, Followers, and their scholars remained apart from it.

Imam Ibn Taymiyyah illustrates this for us in his statement: "The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, had the fewest trials of any generation after them, for the further an era is removed from Prophethood, the more division and disagreement increase." Thus this did not happen until, during the caliphate of Uthman, people were killed and the community split, and two contrary heresies arose at the same time: the heresy of the Khawarij, who declared people disbelievers on account of sin, and the heresy of the Rafida, who claim [some figure's] imamate, infallibility, and prophethood, or [even] his divinity...

[Arabic academic text, translated for reference] ...may Allah be pleased with him, because he was the caliph to whom the community gave allegiance after the murder of Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him. Mu'awiyah's faction rose up demanding retribution for Uthman's blood, and called for the pursuit of the caliphate and for governance following the arbitration (tahkim). The Khawarij were a group among the followers of the Commander of the Faithful [Ali] who rebelled against him because he had accepted arbitration, and they cried out, "No judgment except Allah's" (la hukma illa lillah). They also turned against Mu'awiyah, because he wished to assume authority over the believers, and this could not rightly happen except through mutual consultation (shura) among them. These were a strong and tough people, among the harshest and most severe of the Arabs, and the Commander of the Faithful, may Allah be pleased with him, fought many bloody battles against them for the whole duration of his caliphate, just as their impact continued to trouble the resting places of the Umayyad caliphs throughout the era of Umayyad rule.

After the martyrdom of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, some among his party (Shia) rose up demanding the caliphate as their right.

Thus arose the parties and sects that took on a religious form, having the greatest impact on the establishment of religious doctrines within Islam. Each party attempted to support what it claimed by appeal to the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and, self-evidently, no party could find in the texts of the Noble Qur'an and the noble Sunnah anything that truly supported its claim. So they interpreted some texts of the Qur'an, and explained away some texts of hadith in ways the texts could not bear; even so, this did not achieve what they aimed for, and they did not find, in what they reinterpreted, any way to distort the Qur'an itself, owing to the great number of its memorizers (huffaz). So instead they resorted to distortion and fabrication regarding the Sunnah, attributing to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, things he never said, and the movement of fabrication grew active over time, until authentic hadith became intermixed with fabricated hadith, and fabricated hadiths appeared regarding the merits of the four caliphs and others among the leaders of sects and party chiefs, then further [fabrications] appeared...
notes: Continuing Arabic academic prose; English rendering above is for readability and should be checked against source. Footnotes at bottom: (1) citing 'al-Sunnah wa Makanatuha fi al-Tashri' al-Islami' p. 89; (2) citing 'al-La'ali al-Masnu'a' p. 248, vol. 2.

Muhammad 'Ajjaj al-Khatib
Assistant Professor at the Faculty of Sharia, Damascus University

The Beginning of Fabrication and Its Causes

First: The Beginning of Fabrication

[Arabic academic text, translated for reference] The prophetic hadith remained pure, untouched by lies, and not subject to distortion or falsification throughout the whole period in which the community's word remained united behind the four Rightly-Guided Caliphs, before it split into sects and parties, and before people of vested interests and base desires infiltrated its ranks. The first spark that led to the numerous disturbances of the first Hijri century was the trial (fitna) of Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, and his martyrdom, which shook the Islamic world tremendously and left the community with grave consequences whose effects have extended down to our present day.

Then, after the trial [had passed], the word of the Muslims gathered once more around the Commander of the Faithful Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. However, events proved stronger than allowing calm and peace to find their way to the state at that time, and this resulted in a major split within the ranks of the community: one part gathered under the banner of the Commander of the Faithful Ali, comprising the people of the Hijaz and Iraq, and the other camp under the Commander of Syria, Mu'awiyah, to whom most of the people of Syria and Egypt had attached themselves.

This division led the community into devastating, consuming wars, and it was not long before it ended in the arbitration (tahkim), which became a cause for the emergence of differing political sects (1), and the masses came to blindly follow...[text continues to next page, cut off at page bottom]

Footnote (1) cites 'Tarikh al-Islam' by Dr. Hasan Ibrahim, vol. 1, p. 268; 'al-Tabsir fi al-Din' p. 6; and 'Fajr al-Islam' p. 256. IN THE NAME OF ALLAH, THE COMPASSIONATE, MOST MERCIFUL

Praise be to Allah, who revealed to His servant (Muhammad) this scripture, and made it flawless. A straight foreward message, to preach the awesome power He posesses, and to deliver good news to the believers who do good works; that they shall receive a generous recompense; they abide therein forever. And to warn those who say that God has begotten a son! They have no certain knowledge thereof, nor did their predecessors (who invented this lie). What a gross fabrication coming out of their mouths! They indeed utter but an abominable lie.

(Qur'an 18:1-5)

English Meanings of the Qur'an: 3
by Rashad Khalifa, Ph.D.

A true understanding of Islam requires, as a minimum, a reasonable understanding of its message, the Qur'an. While many people acquire a distorted picture of the religion by observing some aspects of the actions, history, or personal conduct of its professed followers, the readers of this series are presented with an opportunity to grasp the basic principles of true Islam. Readers who are familiar with the various Qur'anic translations will appreciate the fact that this is the first English rendering of the Qur'an's meanings by a Muslim Arab. It is being printed for the first time.

Sura Al-Baqarah (The Heifer) 2:99-187

In the Name of Allah, the Compassionate, most Merciful
(The Distortion of Previous Scripture)

99 We reveal to you herein (O Muhammad) clear verses; only the wicked shall reject them.
100 Is it ever so that whenever they make a covenant, some of them would disregard it? Indeed, most of them do not believe.
101 Thus, when a messenger from God came to them, though confirming their own scripture, some of those who received previous scripture rejected this scripture of God behind their backs as if they know not.
102 They followed instead what the devils have distorted for them such as the magic powers of Solomon. It was not Solomon who abused such powers; it was the devils who abused them. Thus, they taught the people sorcery as revealed through the two angels Harut and Marut. However, these two did not teach anyone except with the admonition that such teachings were a test; that no one shall abuse them. But they use this knowledge in such evil things as breaking up marriages. They can never hurt anyone, however, except by God's leave. They learn only what harms them, not what benefits them, and they fully realize that whoever follows such distortions gets no share in the hereafter. Miserable indeed is what they sold their souls for, if they only know.
notes: Introduction to Rashad Khalifa's English translation series and the start of Sura Al-Baqarah verses 99-102. Footer reads 'ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4): 248-266'.

They do not even follow each other's Qiblah. Surely, if you ever follow their wishes, after this knowledge has come to you, you would be among the wrong-doers.

arabic_segments.raw_text: سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التى كانوا عليها قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدى من يشاء إلى صرط مستقيم . وكذلك جعلنكم أمة وسطا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا وما جعلنا القبلة التى كنت عليها إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه وإن كانت لكبيرة إلا على الذين هدى الله وما كان الله ليضيع إيمنكم إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم . قد نرى تقلب وجهك فى السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ماكنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره وإن الذين أوتوا الكتب ليعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وما الله بغفل عما يعملون . ولئن أتيت الذين أوتوا الكتب بكل ءاية ماتبعوا قبلتك وماأنت بتابع قبلتهم وما بعضهم بتابع قبلة بعض ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم من بعد ماجاءك من العلم إنك إذا لمن الظلمين . الذين ءاتينهم الكتب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون . الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين . ولكل وجهة هو موليها فاستبقوا الخيرت أين ما تكونوا يأت بكم الله جميعا إن الله على كل شئ قدير . ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وإنه للحق من ربك وما الله بغفل عما تعملون

notes: Ornate Qur'an mushaf page continuing Sura Al-Baqarah, corresponding to the English translation of verses roughly 137-159 printed on surrounding pages. Mushaf page marker at bottom reads Arabic numeral 17.

SURA AL-BAQARAH

146 Those to whom We have given previous scripture recognize the truth herein just as they recognize their own children. But, surely, some of them conceal the truth knowingly.
147 This is the truth from your Lord; you shall not have any doubts about it.
148 To each is a direction to which he turns, you shall turn eagerly towards the good works. Wherever you might be, Allah will bring you all. Surely, Allah is Omnipotent.
149 Wherever you may go (O Muhammad) you shall turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. This is the truth from your Lord, and Allah is never unaware of anything you do.
150 Wherever you may go (O Muhammad) you shall turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you might be (O believers), you shall turn your faces towards it. Thus, other people will have no argument against you, except those among them who are unjust; do not fear them, and fear Me. Thus do I complete My favors to you, and to render you rightly guided.
151 Other favors included Our raising of a messenger from amongst you to recite for you Our revelations, and to teach you the scripture and the wisdom, and to teach you things you never knew.
152 Therefore, you shall commemorate Me; I will then commemorate you; you shall be thankful to Me; do not be unappreciative.

(The Believers Must be Put to the Test)

153 O you who believe, you shall resort to steadfastness and the salat prayers. Surely, Allah is with those who steadfastly persevere.
154 Do not consider those who are killed in the cause of Allah to be dead. Nay, they are alive, but you perceive not.
155 We will put you to the test by means of some fear, hunger, and loss of monies and lives and crops. Give the good news to those who steadfastly persevere.
156 When a disaster befalls them they say, "We belong to Allah, and to Him we shall return."
157 These shall receive exaltations from their Lord, and mercy; these are the rightly guided ones.

(Rituals of Hajj)

158 The knolls of Safa and Marwah are among the sacred altars of God. Thus, whoever observes the pilgrimage to Mecca, or observe the 'Umrah visitation, shall encircle them. Whoever volunteers more good works, surely, Allah is appreciative thereof, fully aware.
159 Surely, those who conceal what We sent down of clear revelations
notes: Diacritics on 'salat', 'Safa', 'Marwah' flattened to plain ASCII (original prints with macrons). Text continues onto next scanned page.

arabic_segments.raw_text: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ماكنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره لئلا يكون للناس عليكم حجة إلا الذين ظلموا منهم فلا تخشوهم واخشونى ولأتم نعمتى عليكم ولعلكم تهتدون . كما أرسلنا فيكم رسولا منكم يتلوا عليكم ءايتنا ويزكيكم ويعلمكم الكتب والحكمة ويعلمكم مالم تكونوا تعلمون . فاذكرونى أذكركم واشكروا لى ولاتكفرون . يأيها الذين ءامنوا استعينوا بالصبر والصلوة إن الله مع الصبرين . ولاتقولوا لمن يقتل فى سبيل الله أموت بل أحياء ولكن لاتشعرون . ولنبلونكم بشئ من الخوف والجوع ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرت وبشر الصبرين . الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه رجعون . أولئك عليهم صلوت من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون . إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن يطوف بهما ومن تطوع خيرا فإن الله شاكر عليم . إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينت والهدى من بعد ما بيّنه للناس فى الكتب أولئك يلعنهم الله ويلعنهم اللعنون

notes: Ornate Qur'an mushaf page continuing Sura Al-Baqarah, corresponding to the English translation of verses roughly 146-171 printed on surrounding pages. Mushaf page marker at bottom reads Arabic numeral 18.

transcription_text:
SURA AL-BAQARAH

and guidance, after We have clarified them for mankind in this scripture, these shall be cursed by Allah; they shall be cursed by all who curse.
160 Only those who repent, reform, and declare this scripture, I will redeem them; for I am the Redeemer, most Merciful.
161 As for those who disbelieve, and die as disbelievers, they merit but the curse of Allah, the angels, and all mankind.
162 Eternally they abide therein; neither their punishment can be commuted, nor shall they be granted respite.
163 Your God is One God. There is no good except He, the most Compassionate, most Merciful.

(The Overwhelming Evidence of God)

164 Certainly, the creation of the heavens and the earth; the alternation of night and day; the ships which roam the sea for the benefit of mankind; the water which Allah sends down from the sky to revive dead land therwith and spread in it all kinds of creatures; the manipulation of the winds; the clouds which are placed between the sky and the earth; all these are signs for the people who understand.
165 Yet, some people set up rivals to rank with Allah, and even love them as if they were Allah. But those who believe are much more sincere in their love of Allah. If only the wrong-doers could envision the punishment which awaits them? They shall then realize that all power belongs to Allah, and that Allah is strict in retribution.
166 Those who were followed shall then disown their followers; they shall see the punishment, and all their ties shall be severed.
167 Those who had followed shall say, "If only we could go back, we would disown them as they now disown us." Thus does Allah show them the consequences of their works; nothing but regrets. They shall never get out of the hellfire.

(All Good Food is Lawful)

168 O mankind, eat from the earth that which is lawful and good. Do not follow the steps of Satan, for surely he is your ardent enemy.
169 He only enjoins upon you evil and vice, and to say about Allah what you know not.
170 Thus, when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah sent down," they say, "Nay, we follow only what we found our parents doing." What if their parents lacked any understanding, and were never guided?
171 The similitude of those who disbelieve is like one who parrots whatever he hears without comprehension. They are deaf, dumb, and blind; they can never understand.
notes: Apparent printing typo preserved as printed: 'therwith' (likely intended 'therewith') in verse 164.

arabic_segments.raw_text: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا وبينوا فأولئك أتوب عليهم وأنا التواب الرحيم . إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار أولئك عليهم لعنة الله والملئكة والناس أجمعين . خلدين فيها لايخفف عنهم العذاب ولاهم ينظرون . وإلهكم إله وحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم . إن فى خلق السموت والأرض واختلف اليل والنهار والفلك التى تجرى فى البحر بما ينفع الناس وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الريح والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض لايت لقوم يعقلون . ومن الناس من يتخذ من دون الله أندادا يحبونهم كحب الله والذين ءامنوا أشد حبا لله ولو يرى الذين ظلموا إذ يرون العذاب أن القوة لله جميعا وأن الله شديد العذاب . إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا من الذين اتبعوا ورأوا العذاب وتقطعت بهم الأسباب . وقال الذين اتبعوا لو أن لنا كرة فنتبرأ منهم كما تبرءوا منا كذلك يريهم الله أعملهم حسرت عليهم وما هم بخرجين من النار

notes: Ornate Qur'an mushaf page continuing Sura Al-Baqarah, corresponding to the English translation of verses roughly 160-180 printed on surrounding pages. Mushaf page marker at bottom reads Arabic numeral 19.

transcription_text:
SURA AL-BAQARAH

(Prohibited Meats)

172 O you who believe, eat from the good things We provided for you, and be thankful to Allah if you sincerely worship Him.
173 He only prohibits for you the meat of dead animals, the blood, the meat of swine, and the meat which is dedicated to other than Allah. However, if one is forced to eat these, without being malicious or deliberate, commits no sin. Surely, Allah is Forgiver, most Merciful.
174 Those who conceal what Allah has revealed in this scripture, and trade it away for a cheap material gain, they eat into their bellies but fire; Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they shall suffer a painful punishment.
175 It is they who chose the straying over the guidance, and the punishment over the forgiveness. Therefore, they will have to endure the hellfire.
176 That, because Allah sent down this scripture bearing the Truth; those who dispute this scripture are in extreme error.

(The Definition of Righteousness)

177 Righteousness is not simply turning your faces towards the East or the West (in salat); but righteousness is to believe in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the scripture, and the prophets, and to donate the money, despite one's love thereof, to the relatives, the poor, the alien, the beggars, and for the liberation of slaves, and to observe the salat prayers and the Zakat charity, and to fufill the promises whenever they are made, and to steadfastly persevere in the face of adversity, hardship, and war. These are the truthful; these are the pious.

(The Punishment for Murder)

178 O you who believe, ordained for you herein is commensuration when imposing the maximum punishment for murder; the free person for the free person, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. However, if the guilty is pardoned by the victim's kin, then he shall pay an equitable compensation. This is an alleviation from your Lord and mercy. Whoever transgresses these limits shall suffer a painful retribution.
179 Commensuration shall be a life-saving law for you, O you who possess understanding, that you may achieve piety.

(A Will Shall be Written Before Death)

180 It is ordained for you herein that when death approaches the one of you, if he is to leave any wealth behind, a will shall be made for the sake of the parents and relatives equitably. This is an obligation on those who are pious.
notes: Apparent printing typo preserved as printed: 'fufill' (likely intended 'fulfill') in verse 177.

arabic_segments.raw_text: يأيها الناس كلوا مما فى الأرض حللا طيبا ولاتتبعوا خطوت الشيطن إنه لكم عدو مبين . إنما يأمركم بالسوء والفحشاء وأن تقولوا على الله مالاتعلمون . وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما ألفينا عليه ءاباءنا أولو كان ءاباؤهم لايعقلون شيئا ولايهتدون . ومثل الذين كفروا كمثل الذى ينعق بما لايسمع إلا دعاء ونداء صم بكم عمى فهم لايعقلون . يأيها الذين ءامنوا كلوا من طيبت ما رزقنكم واشكروا لله إن كنتم إياه تعبدون . إنما حرم عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل به لغير الله فمن اضطر غير باغ ولاعاد فلا إثم عليه إن الله غفور رحيم . إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزل الله من الكتب ويشترون به ثمنا قليلا أولئك مايأكلون فى بطونهم إلا النار ولايكلمهم الله يوم القيمة ولايزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم . أولئك الذين اشتروا الضللة بالهدى والعذاب بالمغفرة فما أصبرهم على النار . ذلك بأن الله نزل الكتب بالحق وإن الذين اختلفوا فى الكتب لفى شقاق بعيد

notes: Ornate Qur'an mushaf page continuing Sura Al-Baqarah, corresponding to the English translation of verses roughly 172-187 printed on surrounding pages. Mushaf page marker at bottom reads Arabic numeral 20.

transcription_text:
SURA AL-BAQARAH

181 If anyone alters a will after hearing it, the sin thereof shall befall those who alter it. Surely, Allah is all-Hearing, all-Knowing.
182 However, if one senses unreasonable partiality on the part of a testator, or sinful injustice, and corrects the will, then he commits no sin. Surely, Allah is Forgiver, most Merciful.

(Fasting is Ordained)

183 O you who believe, fasting is ordained for you herein, as it was ordained for those before you, that you may observe piety.
184 A specific number of days is assigned for fasting; if any of you is ill or travelling during these days, he may fast an equal number of other days. As for those unable to fast at all, they shall expiate by feeding one poor person for each day; whoever volunteers to feed more, it would be better for him. But fasting is best for you, if you only know.
185 The month of Ramadan is the one wherein the Qur'an was revealed for the guidance of mankind; to provide a clear message and the statute book. Therefore, anyone of you who witnesses this month shall fast therein. If one is ill or travelling, he may fast an equal number of other days. Allah wants for you ease, rather than hardship; you shall fast the full assigned number of days; you shall exalt Allah for guiding you; you shall be appreciative.
186 If my servants ask you about Me, I am near. I respond to the call of any caller who calls on Me. Therefore, they shall respond to Me, and believe in Me, that they may be rightly directed.
187 Permitted to you is sexual intercourse with your women during the night of fasting; they are your confidantes, and you are their confidants. Allah knows that you used to wrong your souls; He redeems you herein, and pardons you. Thus, you may have intercourse with them, seeking what Allah has ordained for you, and you may eat and drink until the white thread of daylight becomes distinguishable from the black thread of night, at dawn. From that time on, you shall complete the fasting until the following night. You may not have intercourse with them if you decide to go in seclusion in the mosque. These are the limits as set by Allah; you shall not transgress them. Allah thus clarified His revelation to mankind, that they may observe piety.
notes: Diacritic on 'Ramadan' flattened to plain ASCII (printed with a macron over the second 'a').
